Area.evidence_source: The existing literature has been dominated by a risk factor approach that has concentrated on trying to identify risk factors pertinent to the aetiology of attempted and completed suicide in older adults. [...] A number of theoretical frameworks offer some pointers to understanding the psychological processes and social circumstances that facilitate a process of adjustment and help foster an experience of healthy ageing given the plethora of losses that can tend to characterise this period of life. Cognitive models of adjustment to ageing (e.g., Baltes & Baltes, 1990; Brandsta¨dter, 1999) indicate that whether a given experience is construed as being a gain or a loss will be determined by the relationship it shares with an individual's personal goals and belief system. The ability to create and maintain a sense of positive meaning in later life may also be important (Dittmann-Kohli, 1990).
